$comment: Registry of every gate exemption in this repository. Consumed by
scripts/tests/test_gate_exemption_registry.py.
MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED, REASONS ARE AUTHORED. scripts/exemption_discovery.py finds
every exemption surface in the tree -- Python constants by name AND by the prose of
their attached comment, Make variables, shell variables, linter config keys and JSON
baselines -- and the meta-test fails in BOTH directions: a surface that is not
registered here, and an entry here whose surface has vanished. This file is itself a
list, and the whole subject of the change that created it is that hand-maintained
lists go stale, so only the judgement in it is hand-maintained.
WHY IT EXISTS. Four exemption lists stated a premise that was false for at least one
member, and in each case the false member was the one the gate most needed to see.
Every one was the same bug: ONE justification attached to a SET, where the
justification is a property of individual members. Read in aggregate -- 'does this
reason hold broadly?' -- all four pass. So the rule this registry encodes is that a
reason answers for one member, and a premise that can be computed is computed.
FIELDS.
kind      exemption        a real carve-out: members escape an assertion
enforced-universe the list IS the enforced set; the risk is omission
prune             build output / gitignored local work, not a carve-out
fixture           test data that matched the vocabulary; turns nothing off
capability        a runtime allow/deny grant, not a gate
turnsOff  what stops being asserted for a member (required, non-empty)
premise   the name of a predicate in scripts/tests/gate_premises.py that the owning
gate evaluates PER MEMBER, or JUDGEMENT when there is genuinely nothing to
compute. JUDGEMENT is not an escape from scrutiny: a reason is then
required, and the ratchets still apply.
reason    required when premise is JUDGEMENT
ratchet   what makes the exemption finite even where the premise cannot be checked:
non-vacuity (it must shield something), count-pinned (it shields only as
many sites as were audited), universe-closure (nothing may sit outside
both sets), staleness (a dead entry fails), prune-meta-test (deferred to
test_repo_walk_guards_prune_local_work.py), or none
ratchetGap required when ratchet is none: what is consequently unprotected. These
are the honest residuals of this mechanism, and they are enumerable --
which is the point. An unmeasured gap is how this class started.
crossReferences  other entries that must be audited with this one. Two exemptions
pointed at each other in comments and two independent surveys audited one
half and never followed the pointer.
premiseWiring  'pending' on an entry whose premise IS computable but whose gate
does not yet call the predicate. It requires a reason and is counted:
MAX_PENDING_WIRING in the meta-test may shrink and not grow. This state
exists so that 'computable but unchecked' is distinguishable from
'nothing to compute' -- collapsing the two into JUDGEMENT is how a
checkable premise stops being checked.
predicateConsidered  {predicate: why it does not settle the question}. Required when
a JUDGEMENT reason invokes the subject of a predicate that exists --
nested stacks, the publisher's build, an installer manifest, test
collection. See the LIMIT below for what this does and does not buy.
THE LIMIT OF JUDGEMENT AND ratchetGap, STATED PLAINLY.
Both are escape hatches, and a mechanism that pretends otherwise would be the defect
it is meant to fix. So, precisely what each is worth:
* A JUDGEMENT reason cannot be checked. No test reads a sentence. What IS checked is
narrower and is the failure mode that actually occurred four times: a reason that
RESTATES IN PROSE a fact this tree can compute. If the wording invokes a
predicate's subject, the entry must name that predicate or set it aside in
predicateConsidered with a sentence. That is a lint on this file, not a claim about
the world -- it never asks whether a template is a nested stack, only whether an
author who wrote 'nested stack' engaged with the predicate that answers it.
* An author can still write a premise the vocabulary does not recognise, and get
JUDGEMENT plus ratchetGap for it. Nothing here stops that, and nothing here
pretends to. The bound on it is quantitative rather than semantic:
MAX_UNRATCHETED and MAX_PENDING_WIRING may shrink and not grow, so the cost of
reaching for the hatch is a deliberate, visible edit to a pinned number in a test
-- which is a review moment, not a check.
* PREDICATE_DOMAIN_WORDING is therefore the thing to keep current. It is the only
part of this mechanism that degrades silently: a new predicate whose subject is
not listed there can be restated in prose with nothing objecting. Adding a
predicate to gate_premises.PREDICATES means adding its wording there too.
* What none of this covers: whether a JUDGEMENT reason is TRUE. That remains a
reviewer's job, and it is why every reason here is required to state a fact about
this tree rather than restate AWS behaviour from memory -- the rule
TRANSPORT_CONTROL_EXEMPT states in its own comment, generalised.
memberKind  What ONE member names: "path", "deployable path" (a CloudFormation
template or a Lambda source tree), "CloudFormation logical id", "Bedrock
model id", "make target", and so on. Required, and not inferred: it
decides which predicates can possibly apply. A "deployable path" exemption
may NOT be pure JUDGEMENT -- whether the parent deploys it and whether one
publish run builds it are computable, and all four original defects
asserted one of them in prose. The rule stops at deployable paths on
purpose: demanding the same of a documentation link-check exemption would
produce boilerplate nobody reads, and a registry that asks for judgement
on noise gets rubber-stamped.
issues    Optional. Issue or PR numbers already addressing this exemption, so a reader
can tell a known-and-tracked carve-out from an unexamined one. Absent means
'nobody is working on it', which is itself information.

Members split by why they are here rather than sharing one reason: the cache and artifact directory names (**/build, **/dist, **/.venv, **/.aws-sam, **/cdk.out, **/node_modules, **/__pycache__) are bare on purpose, since such a directory is build output wherever it sits, while the two named paths under feature-platform/idp-data-generator are specific staged trees and each carries its own reason and its own computed premise in scripts/tests/test_pyright_config.py::STAGED_BUILD_OUTPUT_EXEMPT. notebooks/**/*.ipynb is a scope decision recorded in TYPECHECK_SCOPE_EXCLUSIONS in the same file. ruff.toml::exclude.turnsOff: ruff's discovery walk, repo-wide, for everything under a named build-output, cache or local-work directory

It restates ruff's own defaults and adds those four. Because the names ARE bare, check_lint_debt.py's bare-name check does not read this array and asserts a property of the walk instead, in both directions: the walk must reach nothing git ignores, and it must reach every tracked .py or .ipynb that no `scope` entry accounts for. That is what closes issue #975 here rather than a list of forbidden names -- the array was otherwise re-openable with every per-file check green, since putting `scripts` back in it drops the walk by 135 files while `ruff check` still prints 'All checks passed!'.

Each names a premise that scripts/check_lint_debt.py evaluates against this tree, per member: the notebook pattern must match nothing but .ipynb and notebooks/_validate_notebooks.py must still be present to check them instead, and the vendored tree must still carry the PROVENANCE.md pinning the upstream commit the re-sync skill diffs against. The per-file lint and format debt this array used to carry now sits in [lint] exclude and [format] exclude, generated from the same baseline. What is NOT pinned is the finding COUNT inside either scope tree, deliberately: a new notebook may add findings without failing anything, and pinning that would red-line every notebook edit.

ruff.toml::format.exclude.turnsOff: `ruff format --check` for the 184 named files, so they are neither reformatted by `make format` nor failed by the format gate
ruff.toml::format.exclude.reason: The files `ruff format` had never been run over, because the trees holding them were excluded by bare name before issue #975. Paying one down rewrites the whole file, so the sweep was deliberately left out of the change that closed #975: five of the seven branches then open were editing 42 of these files and a repo-wide reformat would have conflicted with all five. Formatting is binary per file, so there is no count to pin and the protection is the delist direction -- scripts/check_lint_debt.py fails when a listed file is already formatted, which is what stops the list outliving the debt. Note the asymmetry with the lint array: `ruff format <path>` spelled out bypasses this list, while bare `ruff format` honours it and skips the very file being paid down.
